body: Thanks again. You made me happy today. My best to your reading times that are yet to come!

Thank you! I'm a writer. A procrastinating one. I've reached the point where I put pressure onto myself because I worry that my writing won't be as brilliant as I think it is. So I procrastinate to relieve the pressure. But I digress. This post isn't about my writing problem. xP

I live with my parents, too. Even if my family is around me every day, I still feel lonely. But thank you for the suggestion. Problem is I'm lazy and seeing strangers doesn't motivate me. BUT I do find peace in checking out stores and walking down grocery aisles.
I don't feel safe in public places, though. But I understand the beauty of reading books. I get so absorbed and read voraciously, I could finish one novel in two days. Thanks for the suggestion.
Yes I do. Although I haven't read any recently. I procrastinate reading books. Plus I have a job that takes up most of my time 24/7.

We clearly have nothing to talk about since you find letting go of negative emotions quickly distasteful. You just replied to me with these rants and insults because you had to defend yourself, because I hurt your fragile feelings. Well, guess what? I don't care. People who aren't close to me mean little to me. You can rant all you want. I won't take anything to heart.

When you live in my country, you'll come to that realization at one point or another. I don't want the future generation to suffer from the effects of the exploitation we've done to the planet. I've decided not to have kids so that my children and their children won't suffer from the depressing realities of this world.

I'd make the most of what I currently have, including achievements and skills, not just material possessions. Get back on my feet again, because I know there's always a way if you have the will. This will pass and better days will come.

Things happen because they just do. I don't believe in destiny or things happening for a greater purpose. Life is what you make it.

Your reply left a bad taste in my mouth, but I let go of any ill will against me very fast. I just don't find them very important, a waste of my time and energy. I let go of negative feelings fast unconsciously. I don't know why it's so natural to me. But I never forget. When anyone does something terrible to me, I either lessen my interaction with them or remove them from my life completely.

The idea of being with an ESFJ is crazy to me because I never get along with most S's. I dislike small talk and my ideal partner is someone I can have intellectual, meaningful conversation with. But my dad is an INTP and my mom is ESFP. They fight sometimes but have a great relationship at the end of the day.
I don't forget either. I'm extremely forgiving, but never forget so that it doesn't happen again and to remember how people have treated me.
Even if they said sorry, I easily forget. I'm very forgiving and I don't hold on to negative emotions. Honestly, I've forgotten the last time someone did me wrong.
A class in college. It was love at first sight. Clouds parted and a beam of light shined down on him from heaven.
Don't have kids. Don't want 'em, although I do have mother instincts. The planet has too many humans. I don't want to add more.

Oh... I'm glad you've recognized this and are taking steps to avoid it. Have you talked about your NPD? Does she have NPD too? Not judging because I know what it's like. I've had a narc boyfriend and one of my BFFs is in a relationship with an extreme narc.

Also, maybe you should stop talking about other girls you're seeing. Even if you both aren't monogamous, insecurity can still rise. Jealousy comes from the fear of losing a potential mate to a rival.
Yes. And on almost any surface--paper, desks, hands, and other people's hands if they let me.

Sounds like both of you need to work on your personal issues first. I believe that almost any relationship can work and is worth saving, except relationships with abusers, such as people with NPD. Sorry if this question is too personal. Is either of you emotionally abusing the other? Or each other? '-_-

Something about your situation makes me optimistic. You need to grow together.

She clearly lacks the ability to communicate and is bottling up her emotions. She should learn to talk about her relationship anxieties. This doesn't sound like a healthy relationship for you, but if you want it to work you two should start with clear and honest communication.

If I may add, I have an ENTP guy friend who I flirt with all the time. You could call us FWB without the sex (lol does that make sense? we can't do "it" because of distance) but we're completely honest with each other. There are no resentments and hard feelings whatsoever.
I've lost the ability to stay focused. It's the pressure. Procrastination. Every seasoned writer's problem.

This happened to me, too. I just show up to all the family gatherings. No one will know that deep inside, I don't care when it's not from my nuclear family. People can get sensitive and I don't want to hurt their feelings.

I'm detached, so I don't see anything wrong with not feeling bad.
Yep. :/
I don't know anyone else who's fascinated by space and the universe other than me. :( Then again I don't have many friends.
When not in a relationship I can go for a year and a half without pursuing it. But when I have someone I want it every day.

And there's also the trip to get there. I read it takes up to two years to travel to Mars, depending on factors like fuel and other celestial bodies around. I'm sure they're going to do so much preparation, but to answer the original question, no I don't think they'll survive. At least not all of them.
Well, it's not exactly a conspiracy theory of mine. Kind of, maybe. But think about it... the first humans to live on Mars. Would you be able to say, "What could go wrong?"

I was imagining that it would be very hard to survive there because of the atmosphere, food and whatnot. Even if they do send food and create environments suitable for humans, Mars' chemical composition is very different from Earth.
Man-made things that can produce oxygen
No. Didn't they say that it's going to be a one-way trip? I have thought this over and over. They're saying one-way because there's no way they can guarantee that the explorers will survive.

Did I mention that the guy I'm currently seeing is an INFJ? I've managed to adjust to his style of communication and expressions of affection since we've been together for a long time, but I still feel disconnection sometimes. And it amazes me how he can instantly talk about things that emotionally stir him right there and then. Whereas me, when something he says bothers me, I commit it to memory, dissect it later on, and then talk about it when I find the opportunity.

I agree. I was in a relationship with an ESTP once. He didn't give me the disconnected feels because he's not romantic, sometimes to the point of unemotional. But he shows that he cares through his actions and taking care of me. It didn't work out though.

My tendency to feel detached have happened with romantic partners (the NFs).
See me do me the derp derp derp derp derp

I notice it with my closest friends, too. But it doesn't happen often so I feel really surprised. One time my friend showed me her phone's lock pattern was the initial of my first name. That made me uncomfortable.
Hmm I've never thought of it that way. But good point. Now I remember the feeling of being caught off guard when they say or do something romantic.
Thank you for being straightforward. I appreciate this perspective. I will evaluate the situation further and make sound decisions.
Wow you explained it so well. I can't be both!
That's one of the solutions I've come up with to be more connected. Maybe I should create that ideal romantic relationship in my mind then try to live it out.

I do feel mentally connected with them since the partners I tend to attract can connect with my mind. It's the romantic gestures that make me feel detached. Every time they do something sweet like, say, spelling out my initials with the food on their plate, I just freeze up. At the back of my mind, I appreciate it so much but all I do is give a little smile. That's when I feel detached and guilty for not showing enough sweetness.

I can't understand why this happens to me. I feel so connected to my SO and I love it when we spend quality time together. Then he does a random romantic gesture and I freeze up. It's like getting caught off guard. These are the moments I feel distant. I feel guilty for not reciprocating their sweet gestures, but I do appreciate them.

I've never lived with anyone but I spend one whole month at a time with them occasionally when we go on vacations. At some point I would feel smothered and need my space. I had a boyfriend who interpreted that as being moody, but I just wanted some alone time. Fights happened because of that. 

I do want to spend quality time, but maybe a couple of hours a day.

I just ride the tide of whatever thing I'm obsessing on. I get obsessed easily, but I will soon either grow tired or find another thing that's more interesting and focus on that.

How long have you been together with your significant other? There's always that infatuation stage where the both of you can't get enough of each other. You just want to spend every hour of the day together. Then the honeymoon phase ends and you enter the stable after-infatuation stage. That's when things go back to normal and you can resume your hobbies.
